overview: Two curved, Gram-negative rods in the same genus with very different disease severity and salt tolerance.
genZNote: V. cholerae causes a flood. V. parahaemolyticus just ruins your seafood dinner.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A curved Gram-negative rod that produces cholera toxin, causing profuse watery diarrhea ("rice-water stools").
aspects.valueB: A halophilic (salt-loving), curved Gram-negative rod associated with raw or undercooked seafood, causing self-limited gastroenteritis.

aspects.label: Salt (Halophilic) Requirement
aspects.valueA: Not obligately halophilic — grows in standard media without added salt.
aspects.valueB: Halophilic — requires added NaCl for optimal growth.

aspects.label: Toxin Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Cholera toxin activates adenylate cyclase, raising cAMP and driving massive chloride/water secretion into the gut lumen.
aspects.valueB: Thermostable direct hemolysin (TDH) contributes to diarrheal illness, generally milder than cholera toxin's effect.

aspects.label: Clinical Severity
aspects.valueA: Can cause severe, rapidly dehydrating diarrhea leading to hypovolemic shock if untreated.
aspects.valueB: Typically self-limited watery diarrhea, abdominal cramps, nausea, and vomiting.

aspects.label: Transmission
aspects.valueA: Fecal-oral, via contaminated water in areas with poor sanitation.
aspects.valueB: Ingestion of raw or undercooked seafood (especially shellfish).

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Non-halophilic, cholera toxin, yellow on TCBS.
